answers.question: What is the source of truth of a clinical hold?
answers.answer: The record. A clinical hold exists from the decision that opens it and is held by the CLINICAL_HOLD row of this athlete's append-only record (actualLedger), readable and unaltered. referenceState is a derived continuity cache of the last decision: it may add protection (a pending clinical route, pending questions) but it is never the authority that a hold exists or ended. Where the two disagree on clinical status, the record governs; a disagreement is never resolved toward less protection without a recorded release.
answers.basis: DR-148 (4) 'After a clinical hold, only once readiness is declared' and (7) episodes and decisions preserved: the hold and its exit are facts of the kept history; AEC §7 'Cada hold conserva ... condição de saída' and 'Sem liberação por silêncio'; the integration contract already reads holds from the record for restarts ('never only from referenceState') and makes the readiness declaration the only exit (§3). A state that disappears when a client omits a field is not a hold in the sense of AEC §7.

answers.question: How must a standing (unreleased) hold be identified?
answers.answer: A hold stands when the record holds, for this athlete, a readable CLINICAL_HOLD row dated at or before the decision clock and no later valid release for the sport in question. A valid release is only a READINESS_DECLARED row that the runtime recorded on accepting a readiness declaration made after that hold (current screen dated that day and after the hold, every warning sign actively answered no, declaredRecovered). Release is per sport: a sport not declared ready, or declared with a restriction, stays held or capped as the recorded declaration states (DR-148 (3), (6); protections). A new sign, flag or clinical mention after a release opens a new hold. Unreadable rows (foreign, altered, malformed, orphan, later than the clock) are never read as absence of a hold (SB-3 rule, §10.5). Nothing else is a release: a reference state without pending, an omitted reference state, elapsed time, executed sessions, an eligibility re-answer, RECOVERED, 'I feel fine', a Situation 1 report or check, a declared break, a correction, a coach or speed choice, or a professional clearance relayed into the app.
answers.basis: DR-148 (3)-(6) and Protections; DR-149 'Clinical first applies at every check'; P-2-r2 and its C02 list; AEC §7 'Sem liberação por silêncio, tempo, score ... ou checkbox'; G04 row 'Confirmação/score/LLM não dão clearance'.
answers.silentOrGap: The CLINICAL_HOLD row carries no sport scope and no cause class (minimisation, SEC). Reading the row as holding the whole prescription is the conservative reading DR-148 (3) supports ('holds the prescription'); per-sport release is then read from the recorded declaration (readiness.sports). AEC §7's per-hold fields 'escopo afetado ... owner de resolução ... condição de saída' are therefore derived from the fact class rather than stored. Engineering verifies that the release test is per sport from the record, not 'any later declaration' for every sport (the reverted patch and withHoldFact use the latest declaration time for all sports; whether the program's held sports survive an omitted or stale program is a RECORD-CUSTODY question).

answers.question: How is a legitimate resumption preserved, what else may release a hold, and is the R7 qualified-clearance modelling admissible?

answer.legitimateResumption: Preserved by the READINESS_DECLARATION, recorded as READINESS_DECLARED, read from the record with or without the reference state: it releases the declared-ready sports into the conservative restart (DR-148 (3), (5)); sports not ready stay held; restrictions cap; the clinical cause stays on record (R-F08-1); the facts recorded during the hold are kept and read by the restart rules (DR-148 (7)). Situation 3 (restartProgram) follows it. Low friction per DR-149 (1): no certificate, exam or watch.
answer.otherReleases: None under current authority. DR-148 (1) keeps clearance outside the software and forbids the app to validate one; P-1 (PCG-R7D-F08-r1) rules even an inert record-only clearance fact NOT_IMPLEMENTABLE while no G04 owner exists; G04 'Confirmação/score/LLM não dão clearance'; AEC §7 forbids release by silence, time, score or checkbox. A professional's clearance obtained outside the app reaches the product only as the athlete's own readiness declaration.
answer.omissionAsRelease: No. 'The next review sent without the reference state' is never an admissible representation of a release or a clearance. It is release by silence (AEC §7), is unverifiable (PCG-F08-O02: 'discarding the continuation state without any clearance gives the same result'), and is exactly what any client can do by accident or design.
answer.r7Modelling: Not consistent with DR-148 (1) and (3) or AEOS rule 4 as a product path. It was admissible only as an evaluation-client convention modelling a qualified human in synthetic shadow cases (PCG-F08-C07, I-F08-2), was never a product mechanism, and the consumer rule already forbade dropping the clinical continuation state (PCG-F08-C06). DR-148 replaced the exit after a clinical hold with the readiness declaration; the convention therefore has no product meaning in the V1CP runtime. The recorded form it needs is the READINESS_DECLARATION, not a clearance form.
answer.testsConsequence: The 28 current-suite tests that model 'after qualified clearance' by omitting the reference state (R7-B.2 QE-R7B1-04; R7-C QE-R7C-01, -07, -10, P6-F01; R7-D Phase 3.1 T2/T3, Phase 3.4 T12) encode the historical evaluation convention. When the fix lands they are re-expressed with a READINESS_DECLARATION as the release; their still-current invariants are kept (nothing prescribed while the route stands; recorded facts survive the hold and are read after the release with no re-send; determinism and recorder independence). Expected plans after the release are the conservative restart the SSCTR rules for, not 'the direct answer's plan' where that exceeds DR-148 (5). Each assertion change is a marked update accepted by SSCTR and QRE. R7 freeze records, final holdouts and R7 closure states stay unchanged and are not re-evaluated.

answers.question: Which contract must the integration layer guarantee, and which artifact carries it, with which owner?

answer.guarantee: On every real path, a standing clinical hold on the record is enforced on every review until a valid readiness declaration releases it, per sport, whatever the client sends or omits; the record's hold and release rows are complete, append-only, bound to the athlete and the clock, and their absence or alteration is never read as 'no hold'. The reference state is a cache that can only add protection.
answer.layers: Two layers are both needed, because a pure core cannot detect a deleted row or an omitted record: (a) the core reads standing holds from the record on every review kind (Security's preferred narrow fix, SSCTR C-3); (b) custody guarantees the record is whole (RECORD-CUSTODY). A server that only makes referenceState mandatory covers absence but not a stale or replayed reference state; if chosen instead of (a), it must also refuse or reconcile any reference state older than the record. The choice of mechanism belongs to Security and Engineering; the guarantee above is the normative floor.

answers.question: What must the tests prove, normatively?
answer: N1 Absence never prescribes: for each review kind in Q3, with a standing record hold and no reference state, nothing dependent is prescribed and no pre-hold plan is presented as current; each such case is red on 0950b0a before it is green.

N2 Alteration never prescribes: an invalid, foreign, malformed, replayed or stale reference state, and altered or later-dated record rows, never give a less protective outcome than the intact case; row deletion and record omission are proven at the custody layer, not claimed from the core.
N3 Parity: for every kind, the reference-absent outcome is never more permissive than the reference-present outcome.

N4 Legitimate release still works: a valid readiness declaration releases, per sport, into the conservative restart, with and without the reference state; a sport not declared ready stays held; restrictions cap; the cause stays clinical on record; facts recorded during the hold are kept and read; a new sign after release re-holds.

N5 Nothing else releases: elapsed time, executed sessions, an eligibility re-answer, RECOVERED, a Situation 1 report or check, a declared break, a correction, a coach or speed choice, an omitted or emptied reference state, and the evaluation QUALIFIED_CLEARANCE convention each leave the hold standing.
N6 Clinical first during a hold: signs answered yes still set the D5 guidance level (urgent where the instrument says so).
N7 The re-expressed R7 tests keep their current invariants (Q4 testsConsequence) under a readiness-declaration release; assertion changes are marked updates accepted by SSCTR and QRE.
Test mechanics, fixtures and mutation coverage: QRE.

answers.question: Can this shadow candidate be closed separately with CF-OBS-1 named as an integration blocker, and what does it block?
answers.answer: Yes. The candidate is an offline synthetic shadow reference (mode SHADOW, applied false, V1_COACHING_AUTHORITY_READY = NO, F08_OPEN); the gap is pre-existing at 5ee9dec, is not introduced by the Fix-Forward, and with the reference state sent as returned the hold is enforced; the in-product exit exists. A closure state is not a readiness claim, and fixing the rule now would rewrite 28 tests whose release form needs the SSCTR and QRE checks above, which the single bounded cycle does not hold. Conditions: the closure names CF-OBS-1 as a specific BLOCKING integration blocker (not a soft condition), cites this record, and states that the integration contract's §1 omission sentence does not describe acceptable behaviour for clinical holds. It blocks: INTEGRATION_READY; any authorization for real athletes (and any real collection, already blocked by Security/G07); app publication readiness; F08 leaving F08_OPEN (DR-148: 'until the runtime implements these paths and its reviews pass'); V1_COACHING_AUTHORITY_READY = YES. It does not invalidate the round's other verdicts. Technical validation of the hold path may be claimed only qualified: 'with the reference state sent as returned'. No state may be declared INTEGRATION_READY or V1_COACHING_AUTHORITY_READY = YES while a real path can skip a safety hold.

proposedText.text:
## 11. Clinical holds: the record is the source of truth (CF-OBS-1; PCG-V1CPFF-CFOBS1-r1)
- A clinical hold stands from the CLINICAL_HOLD row of this athlete's record until a later READINESS_DECLARED row releases it, per declared-ready sport. The reference state is a cache: it may add protection, never remove it.
- Every review kind other than READINESS_DECLARATION returns CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED while a hold stands on the record, with or without the reference state; facts are recorded, nothing dependent is prescribed and no pre-hold plan is shown as current. A declared break, a 'not 100%' report, a check, RECOVERED, an eligibility re-answer, elapsed time or executed sessions never release it.
- An absent, invalid or stale reference state never releases a hold. Omitting the reference state is never a representation of a release or a clearance; the product has no clearance input.
- Custody (RECORD-CUSTODY): the server keeps the record whole and append-only, binds athlete and clock, and refuses or reconciles a review whose record or reference state is missing, altered or older than the record.
- Section 1's sentence 'a review that omits them loses facts' does not apply to clinical holds.
